title: Quick Analytics Maturity Scan
description: 24 high-signal questions answerable by a CTO in 10 minutes

questions.questionText: Does your bank have a Board-approved analytics strategy with defined KPIs?

levelDescriptions.1: No analytics strategy exists. Decisions are purely intuition-based.
levelDescriptions.2: Informal analytics goals discussed but no documented strategy.
levelDescriptions.3: Board-approved analytics strategy exists with annual review cycle.
levelDescriptions.4: Analytics strategy drives budget allocation and is linked to business KPIs.
levelDescriptions.5: Analytics strategy is embedded in enterprise strategy with real-time performance tracking.

questions.questionText: Are analytics insights regularly used in executive decision-making?

levelDescriptions.1: Executives rely on gut feeling and anecdotal evidence.
levelDescriptions.2: Basic MIS reports are shared but rarely influence decisions.
levelDescriptions.3: Dashboards reviewed in monthly management meetings.
levelDescriptions.4: Analytics-driven recommendations are standard in strategy sessions.
levelDescriptions.5: Real-time analytics are embedded in all executive workflows.

questions.questionText: Can you quantify the revenue impact of your analytics investments?

levelDescriptions.1: No measurement of analytics ROI exists.
levelDescriptions.2: Anecdotal evidence of value but no formal measurement.
levelDescriptions.3: Basic ROI tracking for major analytics projects.
levelDescriptions.4: Comprehensive analytics P&L with attributed revenue impact.
levelDescriptions.5: Continuous ROI optimization with automated attribution models.

questions.questionText: Do you have a dedicated analytics team with defined roles and career paths?

levelDescriptions.1: No dedicated analytics roles. IT handles ad-hoc reporting.
levelDescriptions.2: A few analysts exist but without clear roles or structure.
levelDescriptions.3: Dedicated analytics team with defined roles and reporting lines.
levelDescriptions.4: Center of Excellence with specialized roles (data engineers, scientists, analysts).
levelDescriptions.5: Analytics talent embedded across all business units with robust career paths.

questions.questionText: Is there executive sponsorship for data-driven transformation?

levelDescriptions.1: No executive sponsor for analytics initiatives.
levelDescriptions.2: IT head informally champions analytics.
levelDescriptions.3: Dedicated executive sponsor (CIO or CDO) with analytics mandate.
levelDescriptions.4: C-suite actively champions analytics with dedicated budget.
levelDescriptions.5: Board-level analytics committee with transformation authority.

questions.questionText: Do business users have self-service access to data and analytics tools?

levelDescriptions.1: All data requests go through IT with weeks-long turnaround.
levelDescriptions.2: Limited self-service for basic reports only.
levelDescriptions.3: BI tools available to trained business users.
levelDescriptions.4: Widespread self-service analytics with governance guardrails.
levelDescriptions.5: Natural language querying and AI-assisted analytics for all users.

questions.questionText: Is there a Chief Data Officer or equivalent role?

levelDescriptions.1: No dedicated data governance role exists.
levelDescriptions.2: Data management is an informal responsibility of IT.
levelDescriptions.3: CDO role established with data governance framework.
levelDescriptions.4: CDO with enterprise authority, data stewards in each business unit.
levelDescriptions.5: Mature data governance with automated policy enforcement and compliance.

questions.questionText: Do you have documented data quality standards and monitoring?

levelDescriptions.1: No data quality standards. Issues discovered reactively.
levelDescriptions.2: Basic data validation rules in some systems.
levelDescriptions.3: Documented data quality standards with periodic audits.
levelDescriptions.4: Automated data quality monitoring with SLA-based alerts.
levelDescriptions.5: AI-driven data quality management with self-healing pipelines.

questions.questionText: Is sensitive data classified and access controlled per SBP guidelines?

levelDescriptions.1: No data classification or access control framework.
levelDescriptions.2: Basic access controls exist but no formal classification.
levelDescriptions.3: Data classified per SBP guidelines with role-based access.
levelDescriptions.4: Automated classification with dynamic access controls and audit trails.
levelDescriptions.5: Zero-trust data access with real-time compliance monitoring.

questions.questionText: Do you have an enterprise data warehouse or data lake?

levelDescriptions.1: No centralized data store. Data lives in operational system silos.
levelDescriptions.2: Department-level data marts with manual ETL processes.
levelDescriptions.3: Enterprise data warehouse in place with scheduled ETL.
levelDescriptions.4: Modern data platform (warehouse + lake) with real-time pipelines.
levelDescriptions.5: Lakehouse architecture with streaming ingestion and unified governance.

questions.questionText: Is your data architecture aligned with an industry reference model (e.g., FSDM)?

levelDescriptions.1: No reference data model. Each system has its own schema.
levelDescriptions.2: Awareness of industry models but no formal adoption.
levelDescriptions.3: Partial adoption of reference model for key domains.
levelDescriptions.4: Enterprise data model aligned with FSDM or equivalent.
levelDescriptions.5: Full reference model adoption with automated conformity checking.

questions.questionText: Can you create a single view of the customer across all channels?

levelDescriptions.1: Customer data is fragmented across multiple systems.
levelDescriptions.2: Partial customer view in CRM but missing many touchpoints.
levelDescriptions.3: Customer 360 view available but requires manual assembly.
levelDescriptions.4: Automated Customer 360 with real-time updates across all channels.
levelDescriptions.5: AI-enriched customer profiles with predictive insights and next-best-action.

questions.questionText: Are predictive models used in any business decisions (credit, fraud, churn)?

levelDescriptions.1: No predictive models. All decisions are rule-based or manual.
levelDescriptions.2: Experimental models in development but not in production.
levelDescriptions.3: 1-3 predictive models in production (e.g., credit scoring).
levelDescriptions.4: Multiple models across domains with model monitoring and retraining.
levelDescriptions.5: ML models embedded in real-time decision engines across all business lines.

questions.questionText: Do you use analytics for customer segmentation and targeting?

levelDescriptions.1: No customer segmentation beyond basic product categories.
levelDescriptions.2: Manual segmentation based on demographics only.
levelDescriptions.3: Behavioral segmentation with campaign targeting.
levelDescriptions.4: Dynamic micro-segmentation with personalized offers.
levelDescriptions.5: Real-time, AI-driven hyper-personalization across all touchpoints.

questions.questionText: Is your anti-money laundering (AML) system analytics-driven?

levelDescriptions.1: Manual transaction monitoring with basic threshold rules.
levelDescriptions.2: Rule-based AML system with high false positive rates.
levelDescriptions.3: Enhanced rules with some pattern detection capabilities.
levelDescriptions.4: ML-based AML with network analysis and reduced false positives.
levelDescriptions.5: AI-driven AML with real-time graph analytics and behavioral profiling.

questions.questionText: Is your analytics infrastructure cloud-enabled?

levelDescriptions.1: All analytics runs on on-premises legacy hardware.
levelDescriptions.2: Some cloud experimentation but core analytics is on-premises.
levelDescriptions.3: Hybrid cloud with some workloads migrated.
levelDescriptions.4: Cloud-first analytics with elastic scaling and cost optimization.
levelDescriptions.5: Multi-cloud analytics platform with serverless processing.

questions.questionText: Can your systems handle real-time data processing for analytics?

levelDescriptions.1: Only batch processing with T+1 or longer latency.
levelDescriptions.2: Near-real-time for a few critical feeds (e.g., ATM monitoring).
levelDescriptions.3: Streaming pipeline for key use cases with minutes-level latency.
levelDescriptions.4: Enterprise streaming platform with sub-second processing.
levelDescriptions.5: Event-driven architecture with real-time analytics across all systems.

questions.questionText: Do you have a modern BI/visualization platform deployed?

levelDescriptions.1: Reports are Excel-based and manually distributed.
levelDescriptions.2: Basic BI tool deployed but limited to IT users.
levelDescriptions.3: Enterprise BI platform (Tableau, Power BI) with business user access.
levelDescriptions.4: Embedded analytics in operational applications with mobile access.
levelDescriptions.5: AI-augmented analytics with automated insight generation.

questions.questionText: How quickly can you deploy a new analytics use case from idea to production?

levelDescriptions.1: 6+ months for any analytics project. No standard process.
levelDescriptions.2: 3-6 months with significant manual effort and approvals.
levelDescriptions.3: 1-3 months with defined analytics delivery methodology.
levelDescriptions.4: 2-4 weeks with automated pipelines and CI/CD for models.
levelDescriptions.5: Days to production with self-service platforms and automated governance.

questions.questionText: Are any business processes automated using analytics outputs?

levelDescriptions.1: All processes are manual with no analytics integration.
levelDescriptions.2: Analytics reports inform manual process decisions.
levelDescriptions.3: Some processes partially automated (e.g., loan decisioning).
levelDescriptions.4: Multiple processes automated with human-in-the-loop oversight.
levelDescriptions.5: Autonomous decision-making for routine processes with exception handling.

questions.questionText: Do you use A/B testing or experimentation for product and marketing decisions?

levelDescriptions.1: No experimentation culture. Changes are rolled out without testing.
levelDescriptions.2: Occasional manual testing with no formal framework.
levelDescriptions.3: A/B testing platform deployed for digital channels.
levelDescriptions.4: Systematic experimentation across products and campaigns.
levelDescriptions.5: Continuous experimentation with multi-armed bandit optimization.

questions.questionText: Can you measure the revenue impact of analytics initiatives?

levelDescriptions.1: No attribution of business outcomes to analytics.
levelDescriptions.2: Anecdotal success stories but no systematic measurement.
levelDescriptions.3: KPI dashboards track analytics project outcomes.
levelDescriptions.4: Formal analytics value framework with quarterly business reviews.
levelDescriptions.5: Real-time value attribution with automated impact measurement.

questions.questionText: Has analytics measurably reduced operational costs in the past year?

levelDescriptions.1: No evidence of cost reduction from analytics.
levelDescriptions.2: Some cost savings identified but not formally tracked.
levelDescriptions.3: Documented cost savings of 5-10% in targeted areas.
levelDescriptions.4: Systematic cost optimization achieving 10-20% reduction.
levelDescriptions.5: AI-driven continuous optimization with 20%+ cost reduction.

questions.questionText: Do analytics insights feed into regulatory reporting (SBP, SECP)?

levelDescriptions.1: Regulatory reports are manually prepared from operational data.
levelDescriptions.2: Some automated data extraction for regulatory submissions.
levelDescriptions.3: Dedicated regulatory reporting system with analytics integration.
levelDescriptions.4: Automated regulatory reporting with analytics-driven insights.
levelDescriptions.5: Proactive regulatory analytics with predictive compliance monitoring.
